class.name: NetwPredict
class.description: This class only holds constants. Set them on [member NetwEntity.prediction]. [codeblock] entity.prediction.archetype = NetwPredict.ARCHETYPE_SOLVER_BODY entity.prediction.recovery_policy = NetwPredict.RECOVERY_POLICY_REBASE_RECOVER [/codeblock] The schedule and simulation mode of an entity are [NetwSimulationHandle] values. [b]Settings[/b] - [enum Archetype] a preset for the other settings - [enum RecoveryPolicy] how a misprediction is corrected - [enum MissingInput] what the server does when an input never arrives - [enum BreachResponse] what happens on an unpredicted contact - [enum Reconcile] whether entities are corrected alone or together [b]Reports[/b] - [enum DriveKind] which input drove the last step - [enum ConsumeAction] what the server did with its input queue - [enum ContactClass] what the body touched - [enum CommandOrigin] where a replayed input came from - [enum ExactVerdict] whether two peers produced the same result - [enum Domain] whether a step is compared exactly or by tolerance - [enum TriggerShape] what asked for a correction - [enum Attribution] what a misprediction is blamed on - [enum Operator] how a correction wrote the body - [enum OperatorOutcome] whether a correction helped - [enum EpisodeState] whether a misprediction is still being corrected

constants.constant: The most ticks a client may predict ahead of the last input the server acknowledged. Past it, prediction holds. See [member NetwPredictionHandle.ack_age_ticks].
The body touched nothing.
The ground reported by the ground sensor.
Static geometry other than the ground.
A moving entity this peer predicts or simulates.
A moving entity this peer does not simulate.
A kinematic or animated body.
This peer guessed the input with [member NetwPredictionHandle.predict_commands].
The controlling peer's own input, relayed through the server.
Nothing has stepped yet.
A new input drove the step.
The previous input drove the step again.
The server held its input buffer, so nothing stepped this tick.
The server had no input queued, so nothing stepped this tick.
A new input drove the step after older ones were skipped.
The input never arrived, and [member NetwPredictionHandle.missing_policy] drove the step.
An input this peer guessed for an entity it does not control drove the step.
No field was past its tolerance.
At least one field past its tolerance can be written by an ordinary correction.
Every field past its tolerance is [method NetwPropertyConfig.teleport_only], so only a teleport can write it.
The server ran a queued input.
The server kept its queued inputs in the buffer.
The server had no input queued.
Not compared yet.
Both peers produced the same result.
The peers produced different results.
The entity does not move.
The last input is repeated.
No preset. Every setting keeps its default. Settings written after an archetype override it, and no archetype sets [member NetwPredictionHandle.breach_response].
A body moved by your own code, such as a [CharacterBody3D]. Sets [constant NetwSimulationHandle.SCHEDULE_TICK], [constant MISSING_INPUT_STALL] and [constant RECOVERY_POLICY_REBASE_REPLAY].

A body moved by the physics engine, such as a [RigidBody3D]. Sets [constant NetwSimulationHandle.SCHEDULE_FRAME], [constant MISSING_INPUT_REPEAT_LAST], [constant RECOVERY_POLICY_REBASE_RECOVER] and [constant NetwSimulationHandle.RESTORE_EXTRAPOLATED].

Restore the server's state and replay every input the server has not acknowledged yet. A [RigidBody3D] or [RigidBody2D] at [constant NetwSimulationHandle.SCHEDULE_FRAME] cannot replay, so it uses [constant RECOVERY_POLICY_REBASE_RECOVER] and warns once.
Restore the server's state and write the correction directly, without replaying.
Do not predict. Simulate only with inputs the server confirmed, and draw the server's state otherwise.
Report mispredictions and correct nothing.

[constant RECOVERY_POLICY_REBASE_RECOVER] for a [RigidBody3D] or [RigidBody2D], and [constant RECOVERY_POLICY_REBASE_REPLAY] for any other body. [method NetwPredictionHandle.resolved_recovery_policy] returns the result.
Correct each entity on its own.
Correct this entity together with the entities its [member NetwEntity.simulation] selects, restoring and replaying them from the same tick.
Keep predicting and correct as usual. A breach is a contact with a moving body this peer does not simulate. Touching static geometry is not a breach.
Stop predicting and follow the server, while still sending input.
The misprediction is still being corrected.
The peers agree again.
Corrections did not help, and the entity follows the server.
Not judged yet.
The error shrank or closed.
The error held or grew.
The correction caused a contact the server did not have.
Every field that asked for the correction is [method NetwPropertyConfig.teleport_only], so the correction could not write it.
Nothing to blame was found. [signal NetwPredictionHandle.divergence_detected] carries an [enum Attribution].
The peers started the tick from different state.
The server ran an input the controlling peer did not send.
The [member NetwPredictionHandle.sensors] read different values.
The peers simulated the entity in different ways.
The state agreed but the raw results differed.
The same input produced a different contact.
Everything going in agreed, and the result still differed.
Nothing wrote the body.
The server's state was restored, advanced to the present.
The server's state was restored as is.
A teleport restored every field.
The body was moved to where it should be now, along a path [member NetwPredictionHandle.transport_corridor] allowed.
The body was reset to the server's state after a fallback.
The first comparison after a reset caught up with the server.
A breach stopped prediction while input keeps being sent.
Only the velocity differed, and it was left to fade.
The whole [constant RECONCILE_JOINT] group was restored to the same tick.
Every input to the step is known equal on both peers, so the results must match exactly.
Some input to the step may differ between peers, so the results are compared by tolerance.
